title: The Garden of the Old Mill House
premise: Seven years after his hands froze mid-concerto and his career collapsed in front of a thousand people, cellist Ivo Blackwood lives quietly restoring gardens at the old mill house he inherited from his grandmother. When his sister demands he bring a partner to the family's harvest reunion, he hires Marlowe Finch, a charming florist who owes him a favor — but the fake date curdles into something real by dessert, and Ivo flees. As the village's autumn music festival approaches, Ivo must decide whether to perform again, forgive the man in the mirror, and claim Marlowe as more than a rental. The story ends with Ivo playing a small, imperfect, joyful set at the festival, Marlowe in the front row, and both choosing to stay.
about_author: Z. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former landscape gardener turned novelist who writes quiet love stories set in decaying English houses. They live in a converted mill with too many roses and a piano nobody plays.

chapters.title: The Letter with the Wax Seal
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A summons to the family reunion arrives, along with a cruel note from his aunt about 'bringing someone this time.' Ivo catalogs his small safe life — tea at seven, roses pruned, no music — and feels the walls of it. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built entirely around avoidance.

chapters.title: A Favor Owed in Peonies
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo visits Marlowe Finch's flower shop, where Marlowe — who once traded him roses for cello lessons neither of them mentions — agrees to pose as his partner. Their negotiation is playful, but Marlowe notices Ivo flinch at a street busker's cello. Emotional beat: fragile hope disguised as a business deal.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. To sell the lie, Ivo and Marlowe spend a Sunday inventing a shared history over the mill house garden. Marlowe asks real questions; Ivo gives rehearsed answers, then one true one about the night his hands failed. Emotional beat: the first crack in the armor, terrifying and warm.

chapters.title: Dessert, and the Truth About It
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. The reunion: Ivo's family is sharper than expected, his mother's grief curdled into control. When Marlowe improvises a defense of Ivo — 'he didn't fail, he survived' — the fake date becomes real for both of them. Ivo bolts. Emotional beat: the high of connection followed by the vertigo of being truly seen.

chapters.title: What the Mill House Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Alone, Ivo finds his grandmother's letters in the garden shed, revealing she too abandoned her music after a loss and regretted the silence more than the failure. Emotional beat: grief reframed — the discovery that survival without living is its own kind of dying.

chapters.title: The Apology Neither of Them Drafted
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. Marlowe confronts Ivo in the rose rows, angry and hurt, admitting the fake date stopped being fake for them long before dessert. Ivo cannot answer; he can only confess the full story of the catastrophic concert. Emotional beat: rupture — honesty offered but not yet received.

chapters.title: Festival Preparations
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The village readies the autumn festival; the committee begs Ivo to play, and his mother arrives to 'help,' reopening every wound. Marlowe, hurt, takes a job decorating the festival anyway. Emotional beat: rising pressure from every direction as the past converges on the present.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The night before the festival, Ivo finally opens his cello case for the first time in seven years and plays to an empty garden — badly, then less badly. His mother arrives, and they have the reckoning the book has owed: she confesses her pressure broke him, he forgives her, and begins forgiving himself. Emotional beat: climax of the inner arc — forgiveness of the person in the mirror.

chapters.title: Eight Minutes of Imperfect Music
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the festival, Ivo plays a short, flawed, luminous set; he stops once, breathes, and continues, and the village holds him through it. He finds Marlowe afterward and asks — not for a favor this time — to begin something true. Emotional beat: the external climax and the choice to belong.

chapters.title: Planting for Next Spring
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue in early winter. Ivo and Marlowe plant bare-root roses in the mill house garden, Ivo teaching cello to the busker's daughter on Saturdays. The last line echoes his grandmother's letters: the garden is not a monument to what survived, but a promise of what returns. Emotional beat: resolution — quiet, rooted belonging.
